body.p: Final Amendment and/or Response Expedited Procedure - TC 3791 Amendments to the Claims: A listing of the entire set of pending claims (including amendments to the claims, if any) is submitted herewith per 37 CFR 1.121. This listing of claims will replace all prior versions, and listings, of claims in the application.

br.br:
1. (Previously presented) An optical vital signs sensor configured to measure or determine vital signs of a user, comprising a photoplethysmographic (PPG) sensor comprising:
a light source configured to generate light that is directed towards a skin of the user, a photo detector unit configured to detect light, wherein the light is indicative of a reflection of light emitted in or from the skin of the user, and
a contact surface configured to be placed against a skin of a user, wherein the light from the light source is directed towards the skin of the user via the contact surface, a force measuring unit configured to measure a force applied via the contact surface of the PPG sensor to the skin of the user, and
a processing unit configured to extract information regarding a blood volume pulse from an AC component of an output signal of the PPG sensor during application of the force applied to the skin of the user and to map the extracted information to a blood pressure value at the measured force applied to the skin of the user via the contact surface of the PPG sensor.
2. (Previously presented) The optical vital signs sensor of claim 1, wherein the optical vital signs sensor is a wrist worn optical vital signs sensor.
3-4 (Cancelled) Final Amendment and/or Response Expedited Procedure - TC 3791
5. (Previously presented) The optical vital signs sensor of claim 1, further comprising a wristband having a cavity in which a distensible membrane is arranged, wherein the membrane can be inflated or deflated by an air pump unit in order to apply pressure to the PPG sensor.
6. (Previously presented) The optical vital signs sensor of claim 15, wherein the force transducer is coupled to the PPG sensor in order to detect the force at which the PPG sensor is pressed against a skin of a user.
7. (Previously presented) The optical vital signs sensor of claim 1, wherein the force applied to the skin of the user is[[]] at least 15 N.
8. (Previously presented) The optical vital signs sensor of claim 1, wherein the blood pressure value is a Mean Arterial Pressure.
9. (Currently amended) A method of measuring or determining vital signs of a user with an optical vital signs sensor configured to measure or determine vital signs of a user, the optical vital signs sensor being a PPG sensor having a contact surface, wherein a force transducer is configured to measure a force applied to a skin of the user, wherein at least one light source generates light that is directed towards a skin of a user, and
wherein at least one photo detector unit is configured to detect light that is indicative of a reflection of light emitted in or from the skin of a user, comprising: applying the force to the skin of a user, emitting light from at least one light source towards the skin of the user and detecting the reflective light by the at least one photo detector, measuring, by the force transducer, force at which the contact surface of the PPG sensor is pressed against a skin of a user,
Final Amendment and/or Response Expedited Procedure - TC 3791 extracting blood volume pulse information from an AC component of an output signal of the PPG sensor and mapping the extracted blood volume pulse information to a blood pressure value at force the contact surface of the PPG sensor
10. (Previously presented) The method of measuring or determining vital signs of a user of claim 9, further comprising:
measuring a blood pressure with an external device, and
calibrating the mapping based on the measured blood pressure.
11. (cancelled)
12. (Previously presented) The method of measuring or determining vital signs of a user of claim 9, wherein only the contact surface of the PPG sensor is used to apply the force to the skin of the user.
13. (Currently amended) A computer program product comprising a non-transitory computer readable memory storing computer program code for causing the optical vital signs sensor of claim 1 to vital signs of a user.
14. (Previously presented) The optical vital signs sensor of claim 2, wherein the force actuator is configured to apply a force to the skin of the user via the PPG sensor.
15. (Previously presented) The optical vital signs sensor of claim 1, comprising a force actuator configured to apply the force to the skin of the user.
Final Amendment and/or Response Expedited Procedure - TC 3791
16. (Previously presented) The optical vital signs sensor of claim 1, comprising a display device that displays the blood pressure value.
17. (Previously presented) The method of measuring or determining vital signs of a user of claim 9, wherein a force actuator applies the force to the skin of the user.
18. (Previously presented) A non-transitory computer-readable medium that includes a program that, when executed by a processor, causes the processor to:
receive a photoplethysmographic (PPG) signal from a PPG sensor that is in contact with skin of a user and detects a reflection of light emitted in or from the skin of the user, receive a force signal from a force transducer that measures a force applied by a surface of the PPG sensor to the skin of the user, extract pulsatile information regarding a blood volume pulse from an AC component of the PPG signal, determine a blood pressure value based on the pulsatile information and the measured force applied by the surface of the PPG sensor to the skin of the user.
19. (Previously presented) The non-transitory computer-readable medium of claim 18, wherein the program causes the processor to control a force actuator to apply the force to the skin of the user.
20. (Currently amended) The non-transitory computer-readable medium of claim 19, wherein the program causes the processor to:
control the force actuator to apply a linearly increasing force to the skin of the user, extract a plurality of pulsatile information from the AC component of the PPG signal and a corresponding plurality of measured force,
Final Amendment and/or Response Expedited Procedure - TC 3791 wherein determining the blood pressure value is based on the plurality of pulsatile information and corresponding plurality of measure force.
21. (Previously presented)The non-transitory computer-readable medium of claim 19, wherein the medium is included in a wrist-worn device that includes the PPG sensor, the force transducer, and the force actuator.
22 (Canceled)
23. (Previously presented) The non-transitory computer-readable medium of claim 18, wherein the medium is included in a wrist-worn device that includes the PPG sensor and the force transducer.
